domain_restrictions: d and r are positive integers.
n is an integer greater than 1.
k ranges over integers from 0 to n - 1.
The q-Pochhammer symbol (u; q)_k is only defined here for nonnegative integer k.
The factor k(d - dk - 2r)/2 is asserted to be an integer in the stated range of k.
q is treated as an indeterminate in the rational-function field Q(q), not as a specialized numeric value.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every choice of positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r <= d, and every integer n > 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the finite sum T_{d,r,n}(q) is termwise identical in Q(q) to the finite sum of A_{d,r,n,k}(q) for k from 0 to n - 1, because the denominator (q^{2d}; q^{2d})_k factors as (q^d; q^d)_k times (-q^d; q^d)_k.
quantifier_order: For any parameter u and any nonnegative integer k, define the q-Pochhammer symbols.
For positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r <= d, and for an integer n > 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, define the two finite sums.
For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n - 1, define the summand A_{d,r,n,k}(q).
In Q(q), the finite sum T_{d,r,n}(q) equals the sum of the A_{d,r,n,k}(q) terms.

witness_dependencies: No existential witness is introduced in the statement.
The equality between the two summands depends on the algebraic factorization of (q^{2d}; q^{2d})_k into (q^d; q^d)_k and (-q^d; q^d)_k.
The integer-valued exponent k(d - dk - 2r)/2 depends on the parity fact that k(1 - k) is even.

statement_nl: Let [m]_q=(1-q^m)/(1-q). For any parameter u and integer k>=0, let (u;q)_k:=∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-u q^j), and let (u,v,w;q)_k:=(u;q)_k(v;q)_k(w;q)_k. Suppose d and r are positive integers with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and suppose n>1 satisfies n ≡ 1 mod 2d. For 0<=k<=n-1, define A_{d,r,n,k}(q):=[3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(-q^d;q^d)_k, where k(d-dk-2r)/2 is an integer because k(1-k) is even. Define also T_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k. Then in the rational-function field Q(q) one has T_{d,r,n}(q)=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} A_{d,r,n,k}(q). Equivalently, each summand is rewritten using (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k.
